title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§8 of the notes). X ⊂ P^r_k is smooth, projective and connected of dimension n over a perfect field k of characteristic p > 0. Y is a smooth hyperplane (or hypersurface) section of dimension n-1. W = W(k). H^i means crystalline cohomology over W.

The vanishing part is E(Y) = Coker(H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y)), and E_DR(Y) is its de Rham analogue.

(8.1.3) is a six-term exact sequence. It comes from comparing, via the universal coefficient sequences 0 → H^i ⊗_W k → H^i_DR → Tor_1^W(H^{i+1}, k) → 0, the restriction maps for X and for Y. Its terms are Ker u_0, Ker u_1, Ker u_2, E(Y) ⊗_W k, E_DR(Y) and Coker u_2:
- u_0 is H^{n-1}(X) ⊗ k → H^{n-1}(Y) ⊗ k;
- u_1 is the de Rham restriction;
- u_2 is the map on Tor_1(H^n, k), i.e. on p-torsion.

The previous page identifies Ker u_2 and Coker u_2, via Poincaré duality, with the duals of Coker u_2'' and Ker u_2''. Here u_2'' : Tors^{n-1}(X) ⊗ k → Tors^{n+1}(X) ⊗ k is cup product with the polarization class, so it is independent of Y. That page also assumes the crystalline weak Lefschetz theorem including torsion: E(Y) is torsion-free.

This page:
(i) Completes the remark that, E(Y) being torsion-free, the Frobenius eigenvalues on E(Y) ⊗ k are the mod-p reductions of those on E(Y).
(ii) Notes (8.3.3) Ker u_0 = 0. This follows from injectivity of H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y) together with Tor_1(E(Y), k) = 0. Grothendieck calls it a 'small luxury': only the last three terms matter 'asymptotically', presumably as the degree of the section grows.
(iii) §8.4: all terms of (8.1.3) carry a functorial p-linear Frobenius. For a finite-dimensional k-space V with p-linear F, let V_ss be the largest F-stable subspace on which F is surjective, hence bijective since k is perfect. Equivalently, F is bijective on V_ss and nilpotent on V/V_ss: this is the Fitting / Dieudonné decomposition V = V_ss ⊕ V_nil. The functor V ↦ V_ss is exact.
(iv) Applying it to (8.1.3) and using (8.3.3) gives the exact sequence (8.4.1):
0 → (Ker u_1)_ss → (Ker u_2)_ss → (E(Y) ⊗ k)_ss → E_DR(Y)_ss → (Coker u_2)_ss → 0.
A handwritten note identifies (Ker u_2)_ss with (^pTors^n(X))_ss and declares it 0 'en vertu de 8.4.4'.
(v) §8.4.2: semisimple p-linear spaces are equivalent to locally free finite-type sheaves of F_p-modules on Spec(k)_et, i.e. to finite-dimensional F_p-representations of Gal(k̄/k) (Lang / Artin–Schreier: V ↦ V^{F=1} over k̄). This category is self-dual, compatibly with k-linear duality.

The next page uses this duality, together with the lemma that H^i_DR → H^i(O_X) is an isomorphism on semisimple parts (via the Hodge spectral sequence), to reach 'Théorème' 8.5. That result is an exact sequence computing (E(Y) ⊗ k)_ss in terms of invariants of X independent of Y and the p-rank-type invariant H^{n-1}(Y, O_Y)_ss.

Purpose: to relate the unit-root part (the number of Frobenius eigenvalues on vanishing cycles that are p-adic units) to Y-independent torsion data of X. The aim is presumably to obtain asymptotic constraints, or a contradiction, on p-torsion in crystalline cohomology as the degree of hypersurface sections grows. This is part of Grothendieck's analysis of whether crystalline torsion behaves like ℓ-adic torsion.
errors: The vanishing of (Ker u_2)_ss = (^pTors^n(X))_ss is asserted only by a marginal reference to an unseen 8.4.4. The claim is non-trivial: it requires Frobenius to be nilpotent on the p-torsion of H^n_crys(X), for n = dim X. That holds for torsion coming from divisor classes, where F acts as multiplication by p. It is not obviously true in general without further hypotheses, so it should be regarded as unverified here.

The whole argument rests on assumed crystalline analogues: weak Lefschetz including torsion (E(Y) torsion-free), Poincaré duality on torsion, and universal coefficients. Grothendieck states these as admitted hypotheses, not proofs. Torsion-freeness of E(Y) in crystalline cohomology is a strong assumption.

Minor: 'assymptotique', 'seul les trois derniers termes', 'indfféremment', 'valeurspropres' are typos/grammar slips. 'Plus grand sous-espace vectoriel stable ... stable par F_V' contains a redundant 'stable'.
Defining V_ss as the subspace where F is 'surjectif' is correct only because V is finite-dimensional and k is perfect, as Grothendieck notes, so F is then bijective there.

ideas.what: Fitting/semisimple decomposition of a finite-dimensional k-space with p-linear endomorphism into bijective and nilpotent parts; exactness of V ↦ V_ss
ideas.modern_name: Fitting decomposition / unit-root vs nilpotent part of a p-linear map (Dieudonné)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dieudonné; Fitting; standard (cf. SGA 7 XXII, Katz)
ideas.where_published: Standard; appears in SGA 7 (Katz exposé XXII) and in Dieudonné's work

ideas.what: Equivalence between semisimple p-linear k-spaces and F_p-local systems on Spec(k)_et (Galois representations over F_p), with compatible duality
ideas.modern_name: Lang's theorem / Katz's equivalence (unit-root F-crystals mod p ↔ étale F_p-sheaves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lang, Dieudonné; Katz (SGA 7 XXII, 'p-adic properties of modular schemes', 1973)

ideas.what: Weak Lefschetz for crystalline cohomology with torsion: the vanishing cohomology E(Y) is torsion-free and Tors^{n-1}(X) ≅ Tors^{n-1}(Y)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (crystalline Lefschetz for hypersurface sections), Ogus; integral versions later

ideas.what: Using Frobenius-semisimple parts of the universal-coefficient / Lefschetz exact sequence to link unit-root eigenvalues on vanishing cycles with p-torsion of X and the p-rank H^{n-1}(Y, O)_ss, with an 'asymptotic' viewpoint in the degree of Y
ideas.modern_name: Relations between Newton/Hodge data (unit-root part, p-rank) of hypersurface sections and crystalline torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related later work: Illusie (de Rham–Witt, ordinarity of generic hypersurfaces, 1990), Deligne–Illusie, Katz

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an exact sequence (completed as Théorème 8.5) linking the unit-root part of vanishing crystalline cohomology of hyperplane/hypersurface sections to Y-independent semisimple invariants of p-torsion in H^*_crys(X). He intends to exploit it asymptotically as the section varies. A torsion-detection method via unit-root parts of vanishing cycles of high-degree sections does not seem to have been pursued in this form.
missed.quote: seul les trois derniers termes de (8.1.3) sont pour nous vraiment importants du point de vue assymptotique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral p-adic Hodge theory (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, prismatic cohomology) now gives tools for the crystalline torsion and weak Lefschetz inputs Grothendieck had to assume. The argument could be revisited, e.g. relating étale F_p-cohomology of hypersurface sections (p-ranks) to crystalline torsion of X.

missed.claim: A marginal note asserts that the semisimple part of the p-torsion of middle-degree crystalline cohomology vanishes ('0 en vertu de 8.4.4'). This amounts to Frobenius being nilpotent on such torsion. The justification is on another page, and the general claim is doubtful or needs hypotheses.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It indicates which statement about Frobenius on crystalline torsion Grothendieck expected. It is checkable against known examples (e.g. Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2, exotic torsion).

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly applies standard tools (Fitting decomposition, Lang/Katz equivalence, universal coefficients) to a conjectural crystalline Lefschetz setup. The strategy of tracking unit-root parts of vanishing cycles to constrain crystalline torsion is a mildly interesting unpublished thread, but not a finished new result.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten annotation above (Ker u_2)_ss reads '= (^p Tors^n(X))_ss' with an arrow. A separate circled pencil note reads '0 (en vertu de 8.4.4)' with a '||' sign below it, indicating the term equals 0.
The margin label before 'D'après la théorie de structure' is handwritten '8.4.2.'
'[-qui-] {+ceux-ci+}': the struck typed word looks like 'qui' overtyped with x's; the handwritten replacement 'ceux-ci' is correct.
'nilpotent' is typed as 'nilpotent' with overtyped corrections; the reading 'nilpotent' is right.
